problem: Prior legged locomotion is mostly blind and reactive (robust recovery on rough terrain) or uses privileged terrain maps/LiDAR, and prior visual navigation uses wheeled robots. No fully learned approach couples visual navigation with visual locomotion that steps over small clutter instead of colliding with it.
motivation: Legged robots can step over household clutter (shoes, toys, cables) without disturbing it, as cats do, whereas wheeled robots struggle or push objects. Low-cost legged platforms lack LiDAR, so egocentric depth is the practical sensor. Rendering depth in RL is slow, so a cheap training pipeline is also needed.
key_idea: Train a depth-based locomotion policy that steps over obstacles (via privileged-map teacher, contact-penalty fine-tuning, then LSTM vision distillation) and a separate Habitat kinematic PointNav policy outputting velocity commands, then co-deploy them zero-shot.
insight: Rough-terrain pre-training gives natural gaits and robustness: without it SR drops from 73.6 to 54.4 and gaits become unnatural. An LSTM memory of obstacles that left the camera view raises SR over an MLP encoder (66.8 vs 73.6) at similar foot collisions. The navigator trained with kinematic control and camera roll/pitch randomization transfers zero-shot to Isaac Gym with a small gap (89.7 in-domain vs 86.8).
method: Stage 1 teacher locomotion: PPO in Isaac Gym on rough terrain (AlienGo), with proprioception plus privileged 11x17 height map encoded by a 3-layer MLP; outputs 12 joint-angle targets for PD control; ~15 min on one RTX 3070.

Stage 2 obstacle fine-tuning: fine-tune in a terrain of random blocks (0.2-0.5 m wide, 0.1-0.2 m high) with a -1 foot-contact penalty and a density curriculum (20 to 200 obstacles per 8x8 m tile, 25 tiles).

Stage 3 vision distillation (Learning by Cheating): 3-layer CNN plus 2-layer LSTM take depth (30° down-pitched camera) and proprioception to regress the frozen policy's map encoding with MSE on on-policy data; ~4.5 h; LSTM remembers obstacles out of view.

Visual navigation policy: ResNet-18 depth encoder plus goal linear layer plus 2-layer LSTM outputs (vx, wz) at 2 Hz; trained with DD-PPO in Habitat on HM3D+Gibson with kinematic teleport control, rewards from Truong et al., 500M steps on 8 GPUs for 3 days.
Sim2sim robustness: roll and pitch of the navigation camera randomized up to ±30° during training to imitate quadruped camera shake.
Zero-shot hierarchical coupling: nav velocity commands (2 Hz) feed the locomotion policy (50 Hz) with no co-training; real AlienGo uses two depth cameras (nav 15° up, locomotion 30° down).

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + LSTM navigation policy (DD-PPO); MLP/CNN+LSTM locomotion policy (PPO + distillation), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Navigation: HM3D + Gibson scans (>1000 scenes), 500M steps in Habitat. Locomotion: Isaac Gym rough terrain and procedural obstacle terrain, then depth-rendered distillation. No web data.
setting.observation: egocentric depth (two cameras) + proprioception + goal distance/heading (egomotion)
setting.action_space: navigation: continuous velocity commands (vx in [0,1] m/s, wz ±60°/s) at 2 Hz; locomotion: 12 joint-angle targets at 50 Hz
setting.simulator: Habitat (navigation training, kinematic control); Isaac Gym (locomotion training and evaluation)
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged terrain map only for the teacher during training; egomotion/GPS-compass goal used)

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 floor plans x 10 start/goal pairs x 5 seeds = 250 runs, ~7 m apart
numbers.extra: navigator and locomotor trained separately in different simulators; 500M steps

numbers_note: Main results are on the authors' own Isaac Gym cluttered-apartment PointNav evaluation, not a standard benchmark; the Habitat HM3D number appears only in the text.
results: ViNL reaches 73.6% SR and 12.08 foot collisions per meter in cluttered floor plans using only egocentric depth. This beats the Rough baseline (privileged terrain map, 40.8% SR, 16.50 collisions/m), a +32.8% SR gain and -4.42 collisions per meter. Sim2sim gap without clutter is small (89.7 to 86.8 SR).
limitations: Evaluated mainly in simulation with small block obstacles; foot collisions per meter remain high (12.08).
The navigator only avoids large obstacles by itself and cannot reason about which small obstacles to step over versus avoid.
Locomotion memory is limited to an LSTM, and the navigator uses ground-truth egomotion.
builds_on: Rudin et al. legged_gym (Learning to walk in minutes)
